active-hours-day.d: Hours per day the user(s) actively send AI queries. Typical: 8 (work day). Heavy use: 12-16.

ai-exposed-content.d: Share of traffic landing on pages that mostly answer explainable or summary-friendly questions.
ai-exposed-content.f: The higher this is, the easier your content is to compress into answers.

ai-inference-cagr.d: Compound annual growth rate of AI inference workloads. Deloitte projects inference will be 75% of AI compute by 2030 at 35% CAGR. Inference MUST be local (latency-sensitive), creating distributed demand across every market.

ai-model.d: Different models have different water footprints based on computational intensity and infrastructure.

ai-queries-per-day.d: Average number of AI prompts per day. Power users: 100+. Casual: 10-30. Developers with Copilot: 200+.

ai-workload.d: Percentage of IT load dedicated to AI/ML training and inference. AI-first facilities: 80-100%. Mixed enterprise: 20-40%.

aig-mean-time-between-failures.d: Average operating hours before a component fails. Higher MTBF = more reliable hardware. Typical values: UPS 100K-300K hrs, server PSU 50K-100K hrs, HDD 1M hrs.

annual-absorption-rate.d: How much new DC capacity the market actually fills per year. Based on historical take-up rates. SG: ~150 MW/yr, ID: ~300 MW/yr, Johor: ~200 MW/yr (optimistic). This is the most critical input — it determines how fast supply gets absorbed.

annual-energy-spend.d: Total electricity cost per year, the single largest operating expense for most data centers.

annual-energy-use.d: Total electricity consumption of the DC including IT load and all overhead (cooling, lighting, UPS losses).

annual-icb-investment.d: Total annual investment in capability building: OEM training courses, certifications (NFPA 70E, refrigerant handling), diagnostic equipment, spare parts inventory, and competence assessment programs. Year 1 typically 60-70% higher than ongoing.
annual-icb-investment.f: ICB Framework: Year 1 ~$85K | Year 2+ ~$50K (10MW facility baseline)

annual-operating-expenses.d: Yearly operating costs including staffing, maintenance, insurance, and non-energy overhead.

annual-turnover-rate.d: Percentage of staff who leave per year. Industry average rose to 21% in 2025. Hyperscalers average 8–12%.

annual-vendor-contract.d: Base annual vendor maintenance contract cost (covering PM visits, priority access, parts discounts). Partially retained under in-house model for OEM warranty work and Tier 4 escalations — typically reduced by 40-60%.
annual-vendor-contract.f: Under ICB: retain ~40% of retainer for Tier 4 OEM access

automation-adoption.d: Level of AI-assisted monitoring and automation deployed. High adoption can reduce headcount requirements 15–30% over 5 years.

average-annual-salary.d: Average annual salary for DC operations staff in your market. Used to compute turnover cost and vacancy impact.
average-annual-salary.f: Turnover cost ≈ 1.5× annual salary per departing employee

avg-build-cost.d: Greenfield construction cost per MW of IT load. Includes land, building, MEP, commissioning. Ranges: $7-8M (VN/PH), $8-10M (ID/MY/TH), $12-15M (SG). AI-ready with liquid cooling adds 15-20%. Used to compute total capital at risk.

avg-revenue-mw-year.d: Annual colocation revenue per MW. Includes power pass-through, space rental, cross-connects, and managed services. SG: $2.5-3.5M, ID/MY: $1.5-2.2M, VN/TH: $1.4-2.0M. Used for break-even and payback calculations.

avg-tokens-per-request.d: Combined input + output tokens per inference request. A typical conversation turn is 500-3000 tokens. Long-form generation can exceed 8000. 1 token ~ 0.75 words

baseline-emissions.d: Total CO2 emissions if the DC used 100% grid electricity with no renewable procurement.

battery-storage-deployed.d: Grid-scale battery storage (4-hour equivalent). Currently ~3 GW in PJM, expected to grow rapidly.

branded-search.d: Share of search visits from users already looking for your brand by name.
branded-search.f: Branded demand is usually more resilient than generic demand.

calc17-avg-build-cost.d: Greenfield construction cost per MW of IT load. Includes land, building, MEP, commissioning. Ranges: $7-8M (Vietnam/PH), $8-10M (ID/MY/TH), $12-15M (SG). AI-ready with liquid cooling adds 15-20%.

calc17-avg-revenue-mw-year.d: Annual colocation revenue per MW of deployed IT capacity. Includes power pass-through, space, cross-connects, and managed services. SG: $2.5-3.5M, ID/MY: $1.5-2.2M, VN/TH: $1.4-2.0M. Hyperscale wholesale is 20-30% lower.

calc17-current-operational.d: Currently live, energized data center IT load capacity. This is the baseline from which demand growth is projected. Source: Cushman & Wakefield H1 2025.

calc17-discount-rate-wacc.d: Weighted average cost of capital for NPV calculations. Reflects risk premium. Infrastructure funds typically use 8-10%. Higher WACC = more conservative valuation. SEA markets typically carry 2-4% premium over US/EU.

calc17-market.d: Pre-loaded with real market data from Cushman & Wakefield, Arizton, and ResearchAndMarkets. Select "Custom" to model a hypothetical market.

calc17-opex-ratio.d: Operating expenses as % of revenue. Includes electricity (40-55%), staff (8-12%), maintenance (5-8%), insurance, land lease, and SGA. Typical range: 55-70% for SEA colo operators. Lower = better margins.

calc17-population.d: Market population for computing per-capita demand density (watts/capita). Used to compare against mature markets like the US (12-15 W/capita) and Europe (4-6 W/capita).

capex-investment.d: Total capital expenditure for DC construction including land, building, power infrastructure, and cooling systems.
capex-investment.f: Typical: $10-18M per MW of IT capacity

climate-zone.d: Hot & Dry: highest cooling demand (+40%). Cold: lowest, free cooling 6+ months/year.

cloud-concentration.d: The share of critical workloads tied to a narrow set of cloud routes or regions.
cloud-concentration.f: High concentration raises application fragility under reroute stress.

co2-avoided.d: Total CO2 emissions prevented through renewable energy procurement. The green premium investment's climate impact.

community-contribution.d: Share of valuable content or interaction generated by users, members, or customers.
community-contribution.f: Community often increases authenticity and trust.

community-impact-factor.d: Social license risk level. 1 = minimal opposition, 10 = active protest/political pressure. Affects regulatory and operational risk premiums.

contract-duration-discount.d: Longer commitments reduce per-year cost through volume discounts. Spot = no discount (1.00x), 3-year = 12% discount (0.88x), 5-year = 18% discount (0.82x).

contracted-response-time.d: Maximum guaranteed time for vendor technician to arrive on-site after dispatch. This drives the Mobilization phase of vendor MTTR. Note: SLA guarantees arrival, not resolution. Actual response may vary ±40% based on time-of-day and resource availability.

cooling-technology.d: Evaporative: ~1.8 L/kWh. Hybrid: ~0.8 L/kWh. Air-cooled: ~0.1 L/kWh. DLC/Immersion: near-zero direct water.

country-market.d: Select the primary market where your facility operates. Hiring score and salary benchmarks adjust accordingly.

country-profile.d: Uses a public-topology resilience baseline for the selected market. It is an analytical profile, not a live routing feed.
country-profile.f: Higher baseline = more likely access to bypass routes and diversified landing options.

country-selection.d: Choose the APAC country to model. Each country has unique electricity tariff structures, grid mix, and DC growth trajectories sourced from IEA, IRENA, and national energy regulators.
country-selection.f: Affects: base tariff, grid carbon intensity, subsidy structure

critical-incident-frequency.d: Total critical incidents per year requiring immediate response. Drives annual downtime and cost calculations. A 10MW colocation facility typically experiences 30-50 critical incidents/year across all infrastructure domains.
critical-incident-frequency.f: Ref: Uptime Institute 2023 — median critical incident frequency for Tier III facilities

critical-spares-availability.d: Percentage of common failure components available in on-site inventory. Directly affects Repair phase duration — missing parts add procurement delay (typically 4-48 hours). Strategic spares program is an ICB Phase 3 deliverable.
critical-spares-availability.f: Impact: Each 10% gap adds ~0.3h to avg repair phase | ICB Phase 3

current-headcount.d: Total filled operations staff positions at your facility. Compared against required headcount to compute the gap.

current-operational.d: Currently live and energized IT load capacity in the market. This is the baseline that represents proven, absorbed demand. Source: Cushman & Wakefield H1 2025.

current-peak-demand.d: Historical peak system demand. PJM's all-time record is ~165 GW.

current-pue.d: Power Usage Effectiveness. Industry average: 1.58. Best liquid-cooled: 1.10. Google fleet: 1.09. Values below 1.1 require full liquid cooling.

daily-inference-requests.d: Total number of inference API calls per day. Used to calculate GPU throughput requirements and monthly compute cost. 100K/day = ~3M/month

data-center-load-growth.d: Incremental data center demand. PJM expects 7-15 GW of new DC load by 2030.

dc-annual-consumption.d: Total annual electricity consumed by the new DC capacity, including cooling and infrastructure overhead (PUE-adjusted).

dc-cooling-type.d: Evaporative towers consume the most water (56% of DCs). Air-cooled and closed-loop use dramatically less but cost more.

demand-growth-rate.d: Annual organic demand growth rate for data center capacity, driven by digital economy expansion, cloud adoption, and enterprise migration. SEA average: 15-20%. Used to model whether absorption will accelerate over time.

demand-response-value.d: Annual revenue from providing grid stability services by adjusting DC load during peak demand periods.

deployment-region.d: Determines regulatory regime (EU EED Article 12 mandatory for EU), grid carbon intensity, energy rates, water stress index, and local labor costs.

deployment-type.d: Cloud = pay-per-use (flexible, higher per-unit cost). Dedicated = reserved instances (cheaper per-unit). On-Premise = own hardware (lowest per-unit, highest CapEx). Edge = device-local (lowest latency).

digital-dependence.d: How much daily economic and social activity depends on stable cloud, broadband, payments, and cross-border applications.
digital-dependence.f: Higher dependence increases sector and public-service fallout.

digital-economy-growth.d: Annual compound growth rate of the digital economy (e-commerce, fintech, streaming, SaaS). Google/Temasek/Bain e-Conomy SEA projects 15-20% for most markets. DC demand scales ~1.5x with digital economy growth.

direct-jobs.d: Permanent full-time positions at the data center facility including operations, security, and management.

direct-traffic.d: Typed, bookmarked, or habit-driven traffic not dependent on the discovery layer.
direct-traffic.f: Higher direct share usually signals stronger brand or repeat behavior.

discount-rate-wacc.d: Weighted average cost of capital for NPV calculations. Reflects risk premium for the market. Infrastructure funds: 8-10%, SEA premium: 2-4% above US/EU. Higher WACC = more conservative assessment of whether the investment returns justify the risk.

diversity-pipeline-investment.d: Annual budget for programs targeting veterans, women, career changers, and apprentices. Models the pipeline expansion effect over the forecast window.

eeq-projection-year.d: Target year for the impact projection (2025-2035). Longer horizons compound DC capacity growth and tariff escalation effects.
eeq-projection-year.f: Tariff growth modeled at 2-5% CAGR depending on country

effective-load-carrying-capability.d: ELCC of renewables — 1 GW solar ≈ 0.15-0.30 GW reliable capacity. PJM uses ~25% for wind+solar combined.

electricity-rate.d: Local utility rate. US average: $0.08. EU: $0.15-0.25. Indonesia: $0.07. Singapore: $0.12. Lower rates favor higher-density deployments.

emissions-with-renewables.d: Net CO2 emissions after accounting for renewable energy procurement (PPAs, RECs, on-site generation).

enterprise-cloud-migration.d: Percentage of enterprise workloads migrating to cloud/colo by 2030. SEA is at ~25% vs US 60%+. Each 10% migration drives ~15-20% of pipeline absorption. Includes banking (OJK-mandated local processing), government (SPBE), healthcare, and manufacturing.

equivalent-trees-planted.d: Carbon offset equivalent expressed as number of mature trees needed to absorb the same CO2.

estimated-tariff-increase.d: Projected percentage increase in residential electricity tariffs due to DC-driven demand growth on the national grid.
estimated-tariff-increase.f: Based on marginal cost of new generation capacity

eu-ai-act-sensitivity-class.d: High-Risk AI requires Article 13 transparency, logging, human oversight. Determines compliance gap count and regulatory weight multiplier.

facility-age.d: Older facilities face higher retrofit costs and structural limitations. Facilities over 10 years typically require significant upgrades for AI workloads.

facility-scale-factor.d: Larger facilities have economies of scale for maintenance services. Small (<2 MW) = higher unit cost, Hyperscale (50+ MW) = bulk pricing and dedicated teams.
facility-scale-factor.f: Affects staffing, spare inventory, SLA tiers

facility-size.d: Total IT load capacity in megawatts. Used to calculate required headcount against industry staffing ratios.

first-party-capture.d: Share of users you can reach directly through email, accounts, saved work, or owned contact channels.
first-party-capture.f: More first-party reach lowers discovery dependence.

floor-load.d: Structural capacity per square meter. Traditional: 1000 kg/m². AI racks (3 ton): need 2500+ kg/m². Reinforcement costs $50-150/m².

forced-outage-rate.d: % of capacity unavailable due to unplanned outages. Winter Storm Elliott saw 25%+. Normal: 5-10%.

forecast-horizon.d: Number of years for the workforce projection model. Longer horizons capture retirement cliff and expansion effects.

forecast-period.d: Number of years to project infrastructure costs forward. Accounts for hardware refresh cycles, efficiency improvements, and traffic growth.

gpu-accelerator.d: The hardware used for inference. B200 is NVIDIA's latest (2025). H100 is the current standard. Groq LPU offers highest tokens/sec but limited model support.

gpu-rack-density.d: Power per rack. Traditional: 8-12 kW. AI/GPU racks: 40-100 kW. NVIDIA GB200 NVL72: 120 kW.

gpu-thermal-density.d: Power density per rack. AI racks range from 20 kW (mixed) to 100 kW (full GPU). Higher density = more cooling cost + grid stress.

grid-carbon-intensity.d: CO2 emissions per kWh from the regional electricity grid. Varies dramatically by country and fuel mix.
grid-carbon-intensity.f: Measured in gCO2/kWh. Nordic: ~20 · US avg: ~380 · SEA: ~500-800

grid-reliability-improvement.d: Incremental improvement to grid system reliability from DC investments in substation infrastructure and demand response.

grid-reliability-score.d: Maps to regional grid stability. 10 = Singapore/Japan grade (SAIDI < 5 min). 1 = frequent brownouts. Affects ARO and failure probability in Monte Carlo.

grid-resilience-index.d: Quality and stability of power supply. 3 = fragile (frequent outages), 9 = robust (Singapore-level). Affects infrastructure investment needs and tariff pressure.

grid-surplus-value.d: Annual value of excess renewable generation fed back to the grid, calculated using E3 methodology.
grid-surplus-value.f: Depends on renewable overbuild and curtailment rates

grid-total-capacity.d: Total nameplate generation capacity of the interconnection.

hardware-refresh-cycle.d: How often GPU/accelerator hardware is replaced. Shorter cycles capture efficiency gains from newer hardware but increase CapEx. Industry standard is 3 years for AI workloads.

hourly-outage-cost.d: Weighted average cost per hour of downtime including SLA penalties, revenue loss, reputational impact, and operational overhead. Varies significantly by client mix and facility tier. Range: $1,000 (enterprise) to $100,000+ (financial services).
hourly-outage-cost.f: Ref: Uptime Institute 2023 — average significant outage cost >$100K

households-equivalent.d: Number of average households that could be powered by the same amount of electricity the DC consumes annually.

hyperscaler-pre-committed.d: Percentage of pipeline with signed hyperscaler LOIs, PPAs, or build-to-suit contracts. Pre-committed capacity is "safe" — it has guaranteed demand. Higher % = lower bubble risk. AWS, Google, Microsoft, and Meta are the primary hyperscaler tenants.

iec-deployment-region.d: Where your inference infrastructure is deployed. Affects energy cost, cooling requirements, and regulatory environment.

incident-frequency.d: Critical incidents (Sev-1/Sev-2) per year causing customer impact or capacity loss. Each costs $100K-$1M+ in direct + reputational damage.

include-upstream.d: Upstream water includes water used for electricity generation (coal, gas, nuclear). Adds ~3x to direct cooling water.

include-upstream-water.d: Electricity generation (coal/gas/nuclear) consumes significant water. Including upstream adds ~3x to direct water. Source: Li et al., Joule 2023.

indirect-jobs.d: Supply chain and service ecosystem jobs created: construction, maintenance vendors, equipment suppliers, fiber providers.

infrastructure-domain.d: Select the primary incident category. Each domain has distinct MTTR phase baselines derived from industry data: Electrical (UPS, PDU, switchgear), Mechanical (HVAC, chillers, CRAH), Controls (BMS, PLC, sensors), Fire Protection (suppression, VESDA, detection).
infrastructure-domain.f: Ref: IEEE 493 Gold Book — category-specific failure/repair distributions

infrastructure-tier.d: Uptime Institute Tier I-IV. Determines redundancy level, expected availability, and baseline MTBF/MTTR assumptions.

interactive-share.d: Sessions touching calculators, dashboards, workflows, or product-like features.
interactive-share.f: Utility tends to be more defensible than passive content.

interconnection-queue-completion.d: % of queued projects that actually get built. PJM historical: <5%. LBNL data confirms most projects drop out.

lc-infrastructure.d: Whether facility has chilled water loops, CDUs, or rear-door heat exchangers installed. Full = complete DTC or immersion ready. Partial = some piping/CDUs. None = air only.

load-factor-benefit.d: Economic advantage of DC's high, steady load factor (80-95%) versus residential's low, peaky profile (30-40%).

long-duration-vacancies.d: Roles that have been open for more than 6 months without a qualified hire. A primary driver of operational risk and cover staff overtime costs.
long-duration-vacancies.f: Vacancy Cost = Long Vacancies × Salary × 0.6 (cover + overtime factor)

market.d: Pre-loaded with real market data from Cushman & Wakefield, Arizton, and CBRE H1 2025 reports. Select "Custom" to model a hypothetical market.

max-single-event-loss-tolerance.d: Maximum acceptable financial impact from a single catastrophic event. Used as SLE cap in ALE calculation and Monte Carlo stress testing.

mean-time-between-failures.d: Average operating hours between critical failures for the selected infrastructure category. Used to calculate system availability: A = MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). MTBF is primarily driven by equipment design, age, and PM quality.
mean-time-between-failures.f: Typical DC: 4,000-15,000 hrs | NASA/IEEE 493 availability framework

mean-time-to-repair.d: Average hours to detect, diagnose, and restore a failed component. Includes spare availability, staff response, and testing. Typical: 2-8 hrs with on-site spares, 24-72 hrs without.

model-architecture.d: Dense models activate all parameters per request. MoE (Mixture of Experts) activates only a subset, reducing compute per token by 2-4x at the same quality level. DeepSeek V3 uses MoE.

model-size.d: Number of parameters in the model. Larger models require more GPU memory and compute per token. 70B is typical for production enterprise inference.

monthly-household-usage.d: Your household's average monthly electricity consumption in kWh. Used to calculate your personal cost impact from DC-driven grid load increases.
monthly-household-usage.f: APAC avg: 200-500 kWh/mo · US avg: ~900 kWh/mo

monthly-sessions.d: Your site's typical monthly sessions before modeled click compression.
monthly-sessions.f: Use a rolling average, not your best month.

multi-model-serving.d: Running multiple models on the same GPU cluster. Improves utilization by routing small queries to smaller models. Adds ~10% management overhead but can improve overall GPU utilization by 20-35%.

national-grid-load-increase.d: Percentage increase in total national electricity demand caused by the new DC capacity.

new-dc-capacity-added.d: Additional data center IT load capacity (MW) planned for the selected country. Each MW of IT load requires ~1.3-1.6 MW total power (depending on PUE).
new-dc-capacity-added.f: 1 MW IT ≈ 1.4 MW total ≈ 12.3 GWh/yr at 1.4 PUE

new-generation-pipeline.d: Approved new generation with financing. Subject to interconnection queue completion rates.

number-of-ai-queries.d: Enter any number. 100 = typical power-user daily count. Global daily AI queries exceed 10 billion.

number-of-ai-racks.d: Total GPU/AI racks to deploy. Hyperscale clusters: 1000+. Enterprise AI: 50-200. Small AI labs: 10-50.

number-of-users.d: 1 = personal use. Set higher for team/org estimates. Enterprise: 500-10,000+. National scale: 1M+.

operating-hours-year.d: 8,760 = 24/7 full year. Most data centers run continuously.

opex-ratio.d: Operating expenses as % of revenue. Includes electricity (40-55%), staff (8-12%), maintenance (5-8%), insurance, land lease, and SGA. Typical range: 55-70% for SEA operators. Used to calculate break-even occupancy and EBITDA margin.

opm-current-pue.d: Power Usage Effectiveness. Google averages 1.10, industry average 1.56. Each 0.1 PUE improvement saves ~6-8% energy costs.
opm-current-pue.f: PUE = Total Facility Power / IT Power

organizational-maturity-level.d: CMMI-style maturity. 1 = ad-hoc/reactive, 5 = optimized/proactive. Lower maturity increases Cost of Immaturity (higher incident costs, slower response).

other-load-growth.d: EVs, electrification, industrial reshoring. McKinsey estimates 3-8 GW for PJM territory.

outside-strait-landings.d: Approximate number of meaningful landing options that avoid the most exposed corridor.
outside-strait-landings.f: More outside landings improve route survival and lower congestion pressure.

p1-critical-mix.d: Percentage of incidents classified as P1 Critical (client-impacting). Critical incidents carry full downtime cost; non-critical incidents carry reduced cost (typically 30% of full rate). Affects financial calculation realism.
p1-critical-mix.f: Cost weighting: P1 = 100% rate | Non-P1 = 30% of hourly rate

per-incident-vendor-fee.d: Direct cost per emergency vendor dispatch including emergency response premium, labor, travel, and standard parts. Does NOT include downtime cost (calculated separately). Excludes retainer/contract fees.
per-incident-vendor-fee.f: Typical range: $1,500-$5,000 per P1 callout depending on OEM and region

phase-duration-spread.d: Coefficient of variation for MTTR phase durations. Low = consistent, predictable repairs. High = wide variance (aging equipment, mixed failure modes). Drives Monte Carlo confidence band width.
phase-duration-spread.f: Low: CV=0.2 (tight band) | Medium: CV=0.35 | High: CV=0.5 (wide band)

pipeline-capacity.d: Total announced + under construction + planned capacity through 2030. Includes both committed (with LOIs) and speculative builds. Source: Arizton 2025-2030.

planned-expansion.d: Additional MW capacity planned within the forecast window. Drives projected future headcount requirements.

planned-retirements.d: Thermal plants scheduled for deactivation. PJM has ~40 GW queued for retirement through 2030.

platform-origin-revenue.d: Share of revenue or leads that begin inside closed platforms such as social, marketplaces, or app stores.
platform-origin-revenue.f: Higher values mean more rented economics.

population.d: Market population for computing pipeline-to-population ratio. Helps contextualize whether the pipeline is proportional to the addressable market or wildly excessive.

power-cost.d: Electricity cost per kilowatt-hour at your deployment location. Auto-filled based on region selection. Adjust for your specific utility contract. US avg: $0.06 | Japan: $0.14

ppa-investment-value.d: Total contract value of renewable energy PPAs over the analysis period. Drives green energy infrastructure investment.

primary-ai-model.d: Different models have different computational requirements. GPT-4/Claude use more resources per query than smaller models. Image generation is the most water-intensive.

priority-sector.d: The sector you care about most when evaluating impact. Different sectors react differently to latency, jitter, and prolonged congestion.
priority-sector.f: Finance and cloud are most latency-sensitive; ports and public services suffer from continuity drag.

process-maturity.d: 1=Reactive, 2=Defined, 3=Integrated, 4=Automated, 5=Optimized. Directly impacts MTTD, automation ratio, and governance integrity score.

qualified-in-house-responders.d: Number of Tier 2+ qualified technicians available for incident response. Used in Erlang-C queueing model to calculate wait probability when multiple incidents occur simultaneously. Understaffing creates hidden queuing delays.
qualified-in-house-responders.f: Erlang-C: P(wait) increases exponentially as utilization → 1.0

quantization-level.d: Reducing model precision from FP16 to INT8/INT4 decreases memory usage and increases throughput at minor quality cost. INT8 is commonly used in production.

query-complexity.d: Simple: short Q&A. Medium: multi-paragraph responses. Complex: long reasoning, code generation. Image: creating images from prompts.

recurring-revenue.d: Portion of revenue from subscriptions, memberships, software plans, or repeat contracts.

redundancy-tier.d: Uptime Institute tier classification. Determines baseline availability, MTBF proxy, and maximum allowable downtime per year.

redundancy-topology.d: N = no spare; N+1 = one standby unit; 2N = fully mirrored parallel path; 2N+1 = mirrored + one spare. Higher redundancy exponentially reduces single-point-of-failure risk.

refresh-frequency.d: How often your tools, data, catalogs, or content meaningfully update each month.
refresh-frequency.f: Live systems usually outperform static pages over time.

region-climate.d: Arid regions need more cooling water. Cool/Nordic climates leverage free cooling, reducing water use significantly.

regional-cost-multiplier.d: Adjusts service pricing based on regional labor rates, energy costs, and market maturity. Americas = baseline 1.00x, Europe +20%, SEA -40%, Australia +15%.

renewable-energy.d: Percentage of renewable energy. Affects upstream water calculation. Solar/wind use minimal water vs. coal/gas/nuclear.

renewable-ppa-capacity.d: Solar/wind capacity contracted through Power Purchase Agreements to meet renewable energy targets.

repair-access.d: Assesses how easy it is for repair ships and permits to reach the fault area.
repair-access.f: Benign, restricted, or contested repair environment.

repair-delay.d: Total time before repair vessels can safely start meaningful restoration work.
repair-delay.f: Longer delay magnifies business loss more than the initial hit itself.

returning-visitor-rate.d: Approximate share of sessions from users who come back repeatedly within a month.
returning-visitor-rate.f: Repeat usage suggests habit, utility, or trust.

revenue-per-1-000-sessions.d: Blended RPM, lead value, or monetized session value used to estimate revenue-at-risk.
revenue-per-1-000-sessions.f: Use your own blended average if possible.

revenue-tier-filter.d: Filter services by their industry revenue ranking. High (#1-40) = critical revenue-generating services, Medium (#41-80) = standard operations, Low (#81+) = niche/specialized.

route-diversity-index.d: A simple 1-10 proxy for how physically separated remaining routes are after the event. More logical routes do not always mean better physical separation.

salary-competitiveness.d: Your salary offering relative to local market median. 100% = at market. Below 90% correlates strongly with above-average turnover.
salary-competitiveness.f: Below 85% = high turnover risk; above 110% = retention advantage

scale.d: Personal: your daily use. Company: 1,000 employees. City: 100K users. Global: ~10 billion daily queries worldwide.

search-dependency.d: Share of sessions that arrive from search engines.
search-dependency.f: High search dependence means more vulnerability to AI answer layers.

service-search.d: Filter the 120 maintenance services by name, description, or keyword. Matches are highlighted in real-time across all visible service cards.

shift-coverage-model.d: In-house team coverage pattern. Affects mobilization time distribution — 24/7 coverage eliminates off-hours gaps. Limited coverage models introduce mobilization variance during uncovered periods.

si-01-country-region.d: Determines labor rates, energy costs, currency, and climate adjustment factors. Tropical regions have ~10-15% higher cooling OPEX.

si-02-critical-it-load.d: Total IT power demand in megawatts. Drives energy cost, staffing requirements, and maintenance budgets. 1 MW = ~200 racks at 5kW avg.
si-02-critical-it-load.f: Energy = MW x 1000 x PUE x rate x 8760

si-03-target-pue.d: Power Usage Effectiveness. Industry avg 1.58 (Uptime 2024). Hyperscalers achieve 1.10-1.20. Tropical locations typically 1.35-1.60.
si-03-target-pue.f: Total Power = IT Load x PUE

si-04-staffing-model.d: In-house provides control; outsourced reduces fixed cost. Hybrid models balance both. 4.2x multiplier for 24/7 coverage per position.

si-05-staff-retention-rate.d: Target annual retention rate. Industry avg ~82%. Each turnover costs 50-200% of annual salary (recruitment, training, knowledge loss).
si-05-staff-retention-rate.f: Turnover Cost = (1 - rate) x headcount x 1.5x salary

si-06-pm-cm-ratio-target.d: Percentage of maintenance that is preventive vs corrective. Best-in-class: 80%+ PM. Industry avg: 55-65%. Higher PM = lower failure risk.

simultaneous-cable-faults.d: The number of major routes impaired within the same corridor. Single faults are usually manageable; clustered faults create capacity squeeze.
simultaneous-cable-faults.f: 1 = resilience test, 2-3 = severe stress, 4+ = strategic degradation.

sort-order.d: Reorder the service catalog. Revenue Rank sorts by industry revenue impact (#1 = highest revenue service). Price sorts by estimated annual cost.

sovereign-ai-demand.d: Government-mandated AI infrastructure + data sovereignty requirements. Includes national AI clouds, public sector digitization, and legally required local storage. This demand is NON-DISCRETIONARY — backed by law, not commercial contracts.

speculative-build.d: Percentage of pipeline built WITHOUT anchor tenants or signed LOIs. These are carrier-neutral facilities betting that "demand will come." Speculative builds are the first casualties in a correction — they bear the most risk. Higher % = higher bubble risk.

staff-count.d: FTE headcount for facility operations. Benchmark: 0.5-2.5 FTE per MW depending on tier and automation level.
staff-count.f: High turnover (>25%) indicates culture or compensation issues

staff-per-mw-ratio.d: Industry average is 3–4 staff per MW. Hyperscale facilities run leaner; colo with high SLA commitments run higher.
staff-per-mw-ratio.f: Uptime Institute benchmark: 3.5 staff/MW for mixed colo

staff-turnover-rate.d: Annual voluntary turnover rate. Knowledge loss from turnover compounds reliability risk over time.

structured-readiness.d: How machine-readable your site is through schema, entities, clean internal structure, and consistent data.
structured-readiness.f: Higher readiness helps citations and agent compatibility.

subsidy-delta.d: Gap between real production cost and industry tariff. Higher delta means citizens subsidize more of the energy cost. Indonesia: ~33%, Singapore: ~5%.

target-latency.d: Maximum acceptable time for first token. Lower latency requires more GPU headroom, increasing cost. Autonomous vehicles need <10ms; chatbots can tolerate 500ms.

tax-revenue-generated.d: Estimated annual tax contribution to local and national government from DC operations, property, and payroll.

team-competence-tier.d: Average diagnostic and repair competence of in-house technicians. Affects Diagnosis and Repair phase durations via a skill factor multiplier. L1 Novice: follow SOPs only. L3 Competent: independent troubleshooting. L5 Expert: root cause analysis, cross-domain.

terrestrial-bypass.d: How much traffic can realistically move over land toward alternative exits.
terrestrial-bypass.f: 0 = weak land bypass, 100 = strong overland relief.

total-component-count.d: Number of identical components in the system chain (e.g., 4 UPS modules, 6 CRAC units). Series chain reliability decreases as count increases — each added component is another potential failure point.

total-it-load.d: Total IT equipment power in megawatts. EED Article 12 reporting mandatory for EU DCs >500kW. Larger facilities have economies of scale.

total-pipeline.d: Total announced + under construction + planned capacity through 2030. Includes committed builds (with LOIs/PPAs) and speculative builds (no anchor tenants). Source: Arizton 2025-2030.

traffic-growth-rate.d: Expected year-over-year growth in inference request volume. Enterprise AI adoption is driving 30-60% annual growth at most organizations.

traffic-prioritization.d: How aggressively operators protect essential traffic. Strong prioritization helps critical workloads but often shifts pain to lower-priority users.
traffic-prioritization.f: Aggressive prioritization improves survival, not overall customer experience.

training-budget-per-employee.d: Annual spend on training, certification, and development per staff member. Industry average is $1,200–2,500. Companies spending $3,000+ see 25–300% ROI via reduced turnover.

water-source.d: Municipal: $4-8/1000 gal. Reclaimed water is cheaper but requires treatment.

weekend-holiday-response-degradation.d: Multiplier applied to vendor SLA during off-hours, weekends, and holidays. Analysis shows vendor P1 response averages 6.8h off-hours vs 3.4h business hours — a 2.0x degradation factor. Affects Monte Carlo tail risk calculations.
weekend-holiday-response-degradation.f: Typical: 1.5x (best case) to 2.5x (remote site) | Source: Section 5.2

workload-pattern.d: Steady = consistent throughput. Burst = peak-heavy (needs headroom, higher cost). Batch = offline processing (can use spot/preemptible, lower cost).

workload-profile.d: Determines power density, cooling factor, failure rate multiplier, and regulatory weight. AI/HPC racks draw 50+ kW vs 8 kW for conventional.

your-annual-impact.d: Annualized additional electricity cost to your household from DC-driven tariff escalation.

your-monthly-impact.d: Estimated additional cost on YOUR monthly electricity bill from DC-induced tariff increases.
